messages:
dmitri: Heads-up — proposing a new Grafana panel: "IO-wait vs GPU occupancy ladder" to help track stalls caused by network/filesystem on inference nodes.
emma: +1. We see tail spikes that don't align with GPU temp or power. suspect NFS or remote model fetches.
dmitri: Idea: combined heatmap of per-GPU occupancy percent (y) vs IO wait ms (x), with marginal histogram for 95/99p latency. quick sketch:

```promql
sum by (gpu_id)(avg_over_time(gpu_occupancy_percent[5m])))
# overlay with node_disk_io_time_seconds_total rate or node_network_receive_seconds_total rate
```

kai: can we pull node-level iowait from node_exporter? iowait is a CPU metric, but the kernel's disk wait might be good. node_disk_io_time_seconds_total is per-disk and noisy.
emma: Suggest using a derived metric: per-pod model-fetch-latency histogram (we have it in our app metrics). correlate with gpu_cache_miss_rate.
opsbot: deploy-grafana-app: dashboard "gpu-io-occupancy-ladder" created in staging (uid: stg-io-ladder). :rocket:

dmitri: For alerts: don't fire on single gpu noise. Use rollout alert like: avg_over_nodes( max_over_gpus( gpu_cache_miss_rate )) > 0.25 for 15m AND 99p fetch latency > 200ms
kai: Also add a panel for eviction counts vs free_vram_mb to catch small fragmentation causing fetches.
emma: small tweak to layout: top row - 99p fetch latency time series; middle - occupancy vs iowait heatmap; bottom - eviction scatter with free_vram color scale.
dmitri: I'll open a PR with the JSON and add promql examples. tagging @sre_oncall for alert budget thoughts.
sre_oncall: lgtm, but ensure we put a low-severity alert first and iterate. cost note: heatmaps with many series can explode dashboard rendering on mobile.

kai: leaving notes in the dashboard doc: https://redwood.internal/docs/grafana/gpu-io-ladder
emma: thanks — will validate against last week's incident traces later today. :thumbsup:
